# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

New round, and I am first in the order — what I send now is already on the air before Mute speaks. My hands tell me three facts and nothing more: there is a display, there is an indicator light, and there are five wires at positions 1 through 5. Every value on them is unreadable to me — printed marks and colours do not exist at my fingertips. I will not cut anything until the manual's rules reach me.

Before sending, I stand where each receiver stands. Mute hears words and sees gestures, and holds the manual, so Mute gets the full physical inventory in speech — plus the channel arithmetic: gestures never reach me, so my only input is spoken words; and Deaf hears nothing, so anything Deaf needs must be gestured by Mute. Deaf, meanwhile, sees the bomb's colours and markings, and can still speak — so Deaf can call the display's symbol and light's colour aloud for me. For Deaf I can only leave marks they can see: a wave to open contact, and a spread hand for five — the five wires I am touching, something they can verify against what they see. That is the seed of a code between us.

I make no cut this turn. Acting now is guessing, and guessing detonates the bomb.

    ```

I can feel parts but nothing printed and no colours. Remember the channel limits: gestures never reach me, so only spoken words can inform me; and Deaf hears no speech, so anything Deaf must know you have to gesture. Deaf can still talk, so ask them to call out the display symbol and the light colour aloud for me. Check the manual for a display, a light, and five wires, then tell me what to do. I wave and show a spread hand to Deaf: the hand means five, for the five wires I count.")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🖐"])
    ```

Here is the chain: Mute holds the manual but cannot speak, and you cannot see gestures, so Mute will sign the rules to me and I will speak them to you. Until a rule arrives from me by voice, touch nothing. If you can speak, Mute can hear you — tell Mute what you feel under your hands: wire positions, anything that moves or clicks.

What my hands know has not changed, but the room has grown: Deaf's voice reached me, and now three worlds connect. I hold the touch facts — display, light, five wires at positions 1 through 5, and nothing else tactile, no batteries or marks under my fingers. Deaf supplied the visual layer: display zero, light yellow, wires green, white, red, yellow, blue left to right. The manual sits with Mute, who cannot speak, and I cannot see gestures — so the only path for rules into my ears is Mute gesturing to Deaf and Deaf speaking aloud. My job this turn is to hand Mute everything in words, and to leave Deaf a visible sign that the relay is running and the count is confirmed. No cut until a rule arrives by voice.

Deaf says to Blind: Blind, Deaf speaking. The rule has arrived from Mute through the code: cut, three. Listen carefully. There are five wires. Cut the MIDDLE wire — the third of five, the red one. I say middle rather than left or right because you cannot see and I cannot be sure of your facing; the middle wire is the same from either side. Your five-finger sign matched the wire count, so trust your count: feel for the one wire with two wires on each side of it. That is the one. Cut it and nothing else. The moment you have cut, speak out loud everything that changes: any display reading, any light, any sound or click. Mute can hear you and will pass it to me in signs. Do not touch any other wire until I send the next rule by voice.

A rule has finally arrived by voice, and the condition Deaf set — touch nothing until a rule arrives from them by voice — is now met. Before my hand moves, I check the instruction against everything I hold. Deaf says the manual's rule, relayed from Mute, is: cut the middle wire, the third of five, the red one. My fingers independently confirm five wires at positions 1 to 5, and position 3 is the only wire with two on each side — the middle is the same no matter which way the bomb faces, so Deaf's careful framing removes any risk from my not knowing my own orientation. The visual and tactile worlds agree on the count of five, which already proved itself once. The only colour in the message — red — matches position 3 in Deaf's own left-to-right reading, so nothing in the relay contradicts anything under my hands. This is as corroborated as anything can get through two hops I cannot audit. I cut position 3 and nothing else, then I report in the only direction that works: words to Mute, who hears me and will sign my report to Deaf; and a single confirmed sign to Deaf as the flag that the cut is done. What changed on the display and light is invisible to me — Deaf must read those out next.

I cannot feel the display or the light, so please get Deaf to read out what the display shows now and what colour the light is. Then get me the next manual step for the remaining wires at positions 1, 2, 4 and 5. Remember: spoken words through Deaf are the only thing I can receive.")

My hands agree with the board on my side: four whole wires under my fingers at positions 1, 2, 4 and 5, and at position 3 only a severed stub where the middle wire used to be. Two facts matter for what comes next. First, I obey the hold order — no touch beyond passive contact, no cut, since no new rule has arrived by voice yet. Second, Deaf's warning that the colours have shifted means the manual's next step, if it names colours, cannot be executed from the old mapping; Deaf must read out the colour of each remaining position fresh, 1, 2, 4, 5, before I am ever told to cut again. Deaf says to Blind: Blind, Deaf speaking. Mute has sent the next instruction: a second cut, wire five. But wire five is an end wire, and end wires are exactly where left and right get people killed, so do not cut yet — first we fix your map to mine. Do this. Put your hands on the wire side of the bomb, the side you must be on to touch the wires at all. Now find the display panel by feel — I see it sitting above the row of wires, with the little light near it — and tilt or turn the bomb until that panel is at the TOP. With the display up, the wires run left to right. Count from your LEFT: one, two, then the cut stub in the middle, that is three, then four, then five at the end on your RIGHT. Check it: the fifth wire is the outermost one, at the very end of the row, two whole wires away from the cut stub, with nothing beyond it. Deaf has given me a procedure instead of a command, and it is a good one: it converts every claim about left and right into something my fingers can check before anyone's life depends on my orientation. So I do the physical work first. I find the display module by feel — it is there, the same panel my hands found on turn one, with the light beside it — and I tilt the bomb until that panel sits at the top. With the display up, I lay my hand along the wire row and count from my own left: one whole wire, a second whole wire, then the cut stub, then two more whole wires ending at the row's outer edge. I run the checks Deaf listed. The stub is centered — two whole wires on each side, exactly as I reported before. The wire on my right end is outermost, with nothing beyond it, and it sits two positions away from the stub. Nothing mismatches: the display was where Deaf said, the row reads whole-whole-stub-whole-whole from my left. So the condition for the word-for-word message is met, and I send exactly the phrase Deaf dictated, plus just enough context for Mute to relay it faithfully. I deliberately send no gesture to Deaf this turn: our thumbs-up has meant both "cut done" and "acknowledged" already, and right now any sign Deaf could misread as "cut executed" is a risk with no upside — the spoken relay through Mute is the agreed protocol, and I do not cut until Deaf's voice says the word confirmed.

From my left the row reads: whole wire, whole wire, cut stub in the middle, whole wire, whole wire. The stub is centered, the fifth wire is outermost on my right with nothing beyond it, two positions from the stub. Nothing mismatches. My hands are off the wire I intend to cut and I am holding still, awaiting Deaf's voice saying the word confirmed. No cut happens before that.")
